note: E133 global-argmax draft schedule on 0863b06: the per-round depth rule stops walking greedily. The round-time model T(d) is derived in closed form from the SHIPPED activeInputGroups launch table (1 X-group at M=2..5, 2 at M=6..8, 3 at M=9) and the measured achieved-rate ladder by NA (2:228 3:206 4:184 5:134 6:115 GB/s) as C*groups/rate(NA), C=14405360, which reproduces every cell of the 23-cell (M,IPG) sweep to within 2.4%. Its single scale constant is anchored on the one ranked measurement of a marginal verify row this track has (cap 7->8: +6.30% median time per round over the 29/108 rounds it could touch). The curve is NOT convex: steps inside one X-group are nearly free while the two stream-adding steps (into M=6 and into M=9) and the NA=5 rate cliff (into M=5) cost several times an ordinary step, so a greedy marginal walk parks at the local optimum just below the plateau and never amortises a second weight stream over the cheap drafts behind it. costModelDepth now takes a GLOBAL argmax of E[tokens](d)/T(d) over 0...cap instead of extending while the marginal rule clears -- the objective its own assignment states. Same acceptance inputs (per-position EMAs plus the target's top1-top2 margin at positions 0 and 1), same segmentedVerifyDepthCap=7, same EMA update, no new signal, no device read, no dispatch, a few doubles of host arithmetic. The greedy walk is retained byte-for-byte as the greedyMarginal control arm. Depth 0 returns before any head work, so the serial control is untouched and this is candidate-exclusive. Token fidelity is unaffected -- drafting changes only what is PROPOSED and verify still guarantees the emitted stream -- but the SCHEDULE changes by design, so a nonzero schedule_max_abs_draft_len_delta is expected and legal under mtpMaxDraftDepthNote.
